full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent No. 2 obtained an ex-parte decree in the Mortgage Suit No. 4 of 2001 in the Court of Artho Rin Adalat, Gazipur against the petitioner. In respect of the said ex-parte decree, the defendant-petitioner obtained a Rule in Writ Petition No. 3083 of 2002, on 03.08.2002, praying for setting aside the ex-parte order dated 06.09.2001 passed in Mortgage Suit No. 4 of 2001 but the Rule was discharged on 20.02.2008. In due course, a review petition was filed being the Writ Review Petition No. 5 of 2008 and a rule was issued on 29.07.2008 upon the respondent-bank. In the meantime, an execution case being the Artho Rin Suit No. 57 of 2008 was filed against the petitioner. As such, the petitioner filed the applications on 20.05.2009 and on 28.05.2009 praying for staying the further proceedings of the execution case but the learned Judge, Artho Rin Court, by his order dated 02.07.2009, issued a certificate under Section 33(5) 9f the Artho Rin Ain and disposed of the execution case under Section 33(9) of the Ain in favour of the decree holder. Being aggrieved, the petitioner filed the present writ-petition. 

 6. It appears that the petitioner filed 2 (two) applications for stay the further proceedings of the execution case, one on 20.05.2009 and another on 28.05.2009 before the concerned Artho Rin Court. In the meantime, the decree-holder, filed an application for issuance of the certificate under Section 33(5) of the Ain. The order dated 02.07.2009 passed by the Artho Rin Court, does not show whether any objection was raised on behalf of the petitioner in respect Of the aforesaid application filed under Section 33(5). The petition under Article 102 in Writ Petition No. 4758 of 2009 was also silent about it. As such, the High Court Division held that in the absence of an order of stay as envisaged in Section 31, the Artho Rin Court can pass an order under Section 33(5) and dispose of the execution case under Section 33(9) of the Ain.
